Where We AreCollection and preparation shape the data that later stages can use

You have a problem worth solving

Data for Your TaskA public dataset can help, but it cannot supply your missing observations

Machine inspection

Which parts need inspection?

Inputs: vibration, current, tool

Label: the inspection result

Collect both for the same part

A useful dataset must connect the input to the outcome

The record is the competenceGoogle: queries and clicks provide feedback that an algorithm alone cannot supply

Search use generates new queries and feedback

The record is the moatQANDA: product use generates observations that a downloaded dataset does not contain

Each student photo records a moment of difficulty and creates another observation

The record is the strategySensor choices determine which aspects of the world become data

Each sensor captures different information

Case study: Waymo vs TeslaDifferent sensor designs produce different training evidence

Collection choiceWaymoTesla Vision
SensorsCameras + lidar + radarCamera-based perception
Distance evidenceLidar range measurementsDepth estimated from images
Data workAlign readings across sensorsTrain and validate visual depth
A measurement and a model estimate need different checks

Constructs and MeasuresOperationalization turns a concept into a measurement procedure

ConstructDefect

→
OperationalizationInspection rule v3

The recorded inspection result

Validity
Does the procedure measure the intended property?

Reliability
Do repeated measurements agree?

Agreement alone does not show that the right property was measured

Unit of AnalysisChoose what one row represents before choosing its columns

One row representsUseful forCan identify a defective part?
One partPart inspectionYes, with part_id
One machine-minuteMachine monitoringOnly with an additional part-level link
One work orderYield reportingNo individual part result
The task determines the grain of the record

Measurement ResolutionA summary can discard information that a later task needs

Context Around the ValueKeep the unit, instrument and event time with the value

Metadata makes the measurement interpretable and reusable

Dataset DocumentationA dataset needs enough context for someone else to interpret and use it

Dataset: part inspectionsDocument with the data
MeaningOne row per part; defect defined by rule v3
CollectionWhich machines, dates and inspection policy
Use and limitsInspection purpose; uninspected parts have no label
MaintenanceNamed owner; update and guideline versions
A datasheet records choices that column names cannot explain

Privacy: Purpose LimitationSpecify the purpose and legal basis before collecting personal data

Failure: safety cameras on the line, later used to score workers. Consent covered safety, not scoring

Caveat: AnonymizationRemoving names does not prevent identification through other fields

Failure: drop the name column and call it anonymous. A public list with matching fields can join it back

02 · Build the Collection Path

Existing RecordsStart with the system that already records the event

SourceRecord to reuseAccess route
Supplier systemPart specification, priceFile export or API
Production systemPart, tool, program, operatorDatabase view or API
Machine controllerSignals and alarm eventsLog file or event stream
The source tells you what was recorded; the interface tells you how to retrieve it

API or CrawlerPrefer an explicit interface; page extraction also depends on the page layout

Answer: Detect a Broken ExtractionA successful request does not guarantee usable records




RunResponseExtracted pricesAction
Before redesign200 OK18Validate fields
After redesign200 OK0Investigate the drop
Selector repaired200 OK18Compare with the last good run

Check counts, required fields and types before accepting the run






  
Copyright: Three GatesAccess, site terms and rights to reuse are separate checks

  

  

  
Failure: a crawled dataset with no documented basis for use. Record the license or the exception you rely on

SoftwareAlarm acknowledged
Instrument the button press

Mount and calibrate the sensor

Apply the inspection guideline
Logging needs instrumentation; physical measurements and judgments need it too

Weak SupervisionLabeling functions provide noisy votes that can agree, conflict or abstain




PartVibration ruleReturn reportImage modelVotes

Labeling functions → label model → candidate training labels
Coverage: 3 of 4 parts receive a vote. Check conflicts on reviewed examples






  
Synthesizing the Rare ClassAugmentation changes an input while preserving its label; generation proposes new examples

  

  

  
Variations supplement scarce real examples; their realism and value still need testing






  
Confidentiality: Trade SecretsCheck whether the data may leave the organization before choosing a cloud service

  

  

  
Failure: pipeline built on a cloud service, then the confidentiality agreement forbids upload. Rebuild inside, or drop that route






  
Security: Attack SurfaceLimit access at every point where data is collected, transferred or stored

  

  

  
Failure: a bucket left public for a demo, indexed by a search engine before anyone notices






  
Collect Reliable Labels

  

  







Sources of LabelsA label can come from deliberate annotation or from an observed outcome




SourceExampleMain collection problem
Human annotationAn inspector judges a partMake the guideline reproducible
Natural labelA delivered shipment has an arrival timeRecord and link the outcome
Model-generated labels remain candidates until checked
Both sources need a definition and a quality check

Demo: Inspector AgreementTwo inspectors each mark five defects among the same 100 parts
B: defectB: pass
A: defect14
A: pass491
1. What is the overall agreement?
2. How many defects did both inspectors identify?




  
Answer: Inspector AgreementCohen’s kappa corrects agreement for chance matches

  

  

    

      

        
B: defectB: pass

        
A: defect14

        
A: pass491

      

      
Two inspectors, 100 parts. Each calls 5 defects

    

    

      
κ = (po − pe) / (1 − pe)

      
po = (1 + 91) / 100 = 0.92 observed

      
pe = 0.05·0.05 + 0.95·0.95 = 0.905 by chance

      
κ = 0.015 / 0.095 = 0.16

      
    

  

  
One shared defect. Adjudicate, revise the rule, measure again





Active Learning: Uncertainty SamplingTarget uncertain cases for learning; audit independently to find blind spots
Partp(defect)What a new label tells us

44730.80Less uncertain under this model
44740.02A random audit can check confident predictions

Goodhart’s LawA reward tied to a reported metric can change how people report it






Reported defects fall while returns stay flat; audit whether reporting behavior changed






  
Fairness: Historical SelectionLabels reflect past access and decisions, not only the property we want to predict

  

  

  
Job performance is unobserved for rejected applicants; rejection is not evidence of poor performance






  
Closing the LoopUse verified outcomes and audits to improve the next collection cycle
